clue.text: Where to replace valuable potted item is problem for gardener

definitions.text: Where to replace valuable potted item
definitions.meaning: in snooker the black, the most valuable ball, goes back on its marked place on the table after being potted
a fungal disease of roses that leaves dark patches on the leaves

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders where to put back a precious plant pot, and that is the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potted' suggests a plant in a pot, but it is a snooker ball sunk in a pocket; the black is worth seven points.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fixed phrases: the snooker table's marked position for the black ball, and the rose disease.

clue.text: Dutch painter sounds German

indicators.note: sounds means the word for German is said aloud to give the painter's name

parts.note: Boche is an old, offensive wartime slang word for a German

explanation.surface: An artist from Holland has a name that sounds German.
explanation.walkthrough: BOCHE is a dated slur for a German, from the World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was a Netherlandish painter of fantastical scenes, so he is a Dutch artist.

clue.text: Face the other way from an attack, and go off

parts.note: a bout is a fit or attack, as of illness
milk that goes off turns sour

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from an assault and walks away.
explanation.definitionFit: To about-turn is the military command to reverse direction and face the opposite way.

clue.text: Ship's ballast taken from Continental shelf off Dover?

parts.note: Dover is a port town in the English county of Kent
a ledge is a narrow shelf, of rock or on a wall

explanation.surface: Ballast for a ship is dredged from the seabed off the English Channel coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental shelf' looks like geology, but only 'shelf' gives letters; Dover stands for its county, KENT, in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentledge is pig iron or scrap carried as permanent ballast in a ship's hold.

clue.text: He makes you fit your own shoe

parts.note: something personal belongs to you alone
a trainer is a sports shoe, the British word for a sneaker

explanation.surface: A cobbler makes a shoe that fits your foot exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like fitting a shoe, but means physically fit; TRAINER is the British word for a sports shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal trainer is a fitness coach who works one-to-one to get a client in shape.

clue.text: Chekhov's Graces?

parts.note: the three Graces of Greek myth were sisters, so the Russian dramatist's version is his play about three sisters

explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's play follows three Prozorov siblings, likened here to the mythical trio of Graces.

clue.text: Beast suffering and wasting away

indicators.note: suffering suggests something damaged and disordered, so the letters of beast are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal in pain is withering away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' signals the anagram of BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabes is a medical term for progressive emaciation or wasting of the body.

clue.text: Asian raised army in desert

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards, from bottom to top
in places the army inside the word for desert

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An Asian force was mustered in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means read upwards; 'desert' is the verb, to betray, not the sandy waste.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tatars are a Turkic people of Central Asia and Russia, so one is an Asian.

clue.text: From north Europe, not cold but hot dish

indicators.note: not means the letter for cold is dropped from the word

parts.note: Baltic describes the region around the sea of northern Europe
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A dish from northern Europe is served hot, not cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a small wok-like pan, a staple of British curry houses.

clue.text: Leather to be had in Slough

definitions.meaning: a material made from the hide of a reptile
a slough is the outer layer a reptile casts off

explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the English town west of London, but it is the skin a reptile sheds.
explanation.definitionFit: Snake hide is used as a leather, and the cast-off skin a serpent sheds is called its slough.

clue.text: He's not taken advantage of Spurs' last free kick

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of the football club's name is used

parts.note: a corner is a set kick awarded when the ball goes out over the defenders' goal line

explanation.surface: A Tottenham Hotspur player failed to make use of a late free kick.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; 'of' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorner spurns or disdains things, so he declines to take advantage of what is offered.

clue.text: Directions to announce a daughter for Abel

parts.note: E and S are the compass points east and south
to tell is to announce or make known

explanation.surface: Instructions for naming a baby girl are given to a man called Abel.
explanation.walkthrough: Abel Magwitch, the convict in Dickens's Great Expectations, turns out to be Estella's father.
explanation.definitionFit: In the novel the convict Abel Magwitch is revealed as Estella's real father.

clue.text: Into prepared hole start to twist sleeper

indicators.note: into puts the starting letter inside the letters of hole
prepared means the letters are worked into a new arrangement
start to means the first letter of twist

explanation.surface: Someone digs a hole and begins twisting a railway sleeper into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeper' looks like a railway tie, but means a place where people sleep; 'start to' takes T from 'twist'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is where guests sleep for the night, so it is loosely a sleeper, a place for sleeping.

clue.text: What a gradient! Get round west a different way

indicators.note: get round means the exclamation surrounds the letter for west

parts.note: an exclamation at a steep slope: oh, the rise!

explanation.surface: A walker gasps at a steep hill and looks for a western route round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a gradient!' is read as 'O the rise!', a cry at a steep slope, which gives O THE RISE around W.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in another manner or differently.

clue.text: Ignore fractions in regular series

definitions.meaning: to drop the part after the decimal point and take the nearest whole number
a recurring sequence, as of visits, drinks or games

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To round a number is to discard fractions; a round is also a set sequence, like a milkman's daily circuit.

clue.text: Fantasies limit Liberal parties

indicators.note: limit means the word for fantasies encloses the letter for Liberal

parts.note: reveries are daydreams or fantasies
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in British politics

explanation.surface: Daydreams cap the number of Liberal Party gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelries are lively celebrations, so they are noisy parties.

clue.text: Point made in a scrum — hit forcefully

indicators.note: made in means the compass point is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a ruck is a loose scrum in rugby, or a crowd
west is one of the four compass points

explanation.surface: A rugby point was scored in a scrum after a hard hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture suggests a try, but 'Point' is a compass point; the answer reads as AWE-STRUCK, struck by awe, hence 'hit forcefully'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck with awe is being hit hard by wonder, so the definition plays on the literal sense.

clue.text: Troop, when ordered, make house available for inspection

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers, when commanded, open a house for inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a military command to the troop, but signals rearranging TROOP and WHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw open a house is to open it up to visitors or viewing.

clue.text: In Scotland, strange new physics lab meeting indifference

parts.note: unco is a Scots word for strange or unusual
CERN is the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva

explanation.surface: A strange new Scottish physics laboratory is greeted with apathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcern is a lack of worry or interest, which is indifference.

clue.text: No end of spite here: doctor, securing conclusion, relaxed

indicators.note: securing means the vet holds the word for conclusion inside

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
an end is a conclusion
relaxed is read as sat back, so the word sat is written backwards

explanation.surface: A doctor at the end of a spiteful dispute finally unwinds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxed' stands for 'sat back', which is read as an instruction, giving TAS; the setter leaves the reversal implied.
explanation.definitionFit: Vendettas are long-running feuds, so they are places where spite never ends.

clue.text: One thing kedgeree has, we hear: poison

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: kedgeree, a British dish of fish, eggs and rice, has rice in it

explanation.surface: Something in a kedgeree is said to be poisonous.
explanation.walkthrough: Kedgeree is a curried dish of smoked fish, egg and rice; 'rice in' sounds like the poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricin is a deadly toxin extracted from castor beans.

clue.text: Meadow is still there; wife's in it, at any rate

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: in it means the letter for wife goes inside the word for remaining

parts.note: stays means remains or is still there
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: The meadow remains; a wife is in it anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Leastways is a dialect or informal word meaning at least or anyway.

clue.text: Test, for example, twice

parts.note: as and say both mean for example, as in a fruit, say an apple
as and say both mean for example, as in a fruit, say an apple

explanation.surface: A test, for example, done twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' asks for two different words each meaning 'for example': AS and SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test, especially of the purity of a metal or ore.

clue.text: Correspond highly?

definitions.meaning: to match or agree, as figures that add up
in a tall manner, the adverb of tall

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful coinage: the adverb from 'tall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts tally when they correspond; the question mark admits the jokey adverb meaning loftily.

clue.text: Pull up, with virtually no distance to spare?

parts.note: an inch is a tiny distance, as in missing by an inch

explanation.surface: A driver pulls up with barely any room to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch is a hauling device, and to winch something is to pull it up with one.

clue.text: Chap's extremely simple for a Nobel winner

parts.note: the chap is a he, and chap's is he's

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters, first and last, of simple

explanation.surface: A man is utterly simple for someone who won a Nobel Prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann Hesse, author of Steppenwolf, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1946.

clue.text: After injury, cut home — body needs it

indicators.note: after means the word for home is placed following the other piece
cut means the word is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: an insult is an injury, as in adding insult to injury, or in medicine a trauma
in means at home

explanation.surface: After an injury, a cut sends someone home, and the body needs care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injury' as INSULT is a medical sense; 'cut' trims it to INSUL.
explanation.definitionFit: The body needs this hormone to regulate blood sugar; diabetics inject it.

clue.text: Squeeze out of train

definitions.meaning: to press juice or liquid out of something
a fast train with few stops

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To express juice is to squeeze it out; an express is a fast train.

clue.text: Dramatist succeeded at first in underhand way

indicators.note: at first means the letter for succeeded is placed at the front

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
John Lyly was an Elizabethan playwright

explanation.surface: A playwright succeeded at first by underhand means.
explanation.definitionFit: Slyly means in a sly, cunning or underhand manner.

clue.text: Fault in horse, note: especially this one?

definitions.text: Fault in horse, note: especially this one?

indicators.note: in puts the word for fault inside the word for horse

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a coat flecked with white
a sin is a fault or wrongdoing
te is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A notice says a fault was found in a horse, and this one in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes Don Quixote's horse, a famously faulty nag; 'especially this one' points to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosinante is Don Quixote's broken-down old horse, so it is a horse notably full of faults.
